label: late-episode drop of z, much deeper after choosing a1 (strongest at D2)
explanation: Update gate z of unit 8 sits near 1 (mean 0.987) and drops only late in the episode (trials ~90-99), mostly at D2. Beyond the per-decile timing baseline, the size of that drop is set by the choice. At D2 after choosing a1, z falls far below the decile mean (down to ~0.35-0.45 at t95-99); after a2 it stays near 0.85-0.9. At D1/GO the drop is deeper when the previous choice was a1, and at D1 somewhat deeper after an unrewarded previous trial. A late-episode ramp (exp((ep_trial-99)/6)) times these choice indicators carries nearly all of the gain (late ramp x a1 at D2 has the largest weight). Small episode-wide terms add that D2 after a1 is lower and D1 after a1->S2 is lower; reaching S1 at D2 slightly offsets. Value, hidden good state and trials since reversal add little. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.57 (dev 0.55), versus 0.16 for the profile additive all ceiling, which lacks the within-decile ramp x choice interaction. Observed-only terms (action is known at D2). Caveat: much of the gain is a timing x choice interaction within the last decile.

issues: Reproduced: the original 8 terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.570. The core claim holds. Using only ramp*D2*a1 plus ramp*D2 gives 0.480, so the a1-at-D2 interaction carries most of the gain. Adding the ramp x prev_action==a1 term at D1/GO and a D1 ramp brings it to 0.548.
The 'deeper at D1 after an unrewarded previous trial' claim is real but small. Adding ramp*D1*(prev_reward==0) moves test R^2 from 0.548 to 0.557 (weight -0.06).

The single exp((ep_trial-99)/6) ramp has the wrong shape. Other taus score worse (tau 3: 0.48, tau 4: 0.53, tau 9: 0.55). Two ramps (tau 6 and tau 2.5) crossed with the same choice indicators reach test 0.640 using timing x choice terms only. So about 0.07 of what the stated terms miss is ramp shape, not new behavioural content.

'Value adds little' is overstated as tested. Adding ramp*D2*value to the 5 core terms raises test R^2 from 0.557 to 0.644 (positive weight: lower value at D2 means a deeper drop). Once the ramp shape is fixed, value adds only about 0.03 (to 0.668). So value acts mostly as a finer end-of-episode clock. Observed proxies such as state==prev_state x prev_reward, state==good, and this trial's reward add at most 0.01.

Misses on the original terms: per-window errors are large in long a1 streaks at t93-99. D2 actual is about 0.37-0.46 against predicted 0.6-0.7, so the model under-predicts the drop. Adding recent-trial a1-count terms did not help (0.569), so this is mostly ramp shape rather than streak length. The aggregate errors by phase x previous trial are small (|mean| <= 0.012; D2 after a1 S2 u is the most over-predicted) and do not form a large systematic class.
The caveat is fair: almost all of the gain is a timing x choice interaction inside the last decile. The explained verdict holds only because the baseline uses decile-level timing.
